question: Why Tibbett Allen left the Board in 1888 is unknown. He was elected for Jefferson District in 1887; the county court issued a rule against him on 3 September 1888 to show cause why he should not be removed for non-residence; he resigned and Frank Hume was appointed in his place on 2 October. The court never ruled, so there is no finding that he was non-resident, and nothing records where he lived. He was the last Black member until William T. Newman, Jr. was seated in 1988. The Black press did not cover it: the Washington Bee carries nothing in any issue from August to December 1888, the Richmond Planet has one digitized issue in all of 1888 and it is silent, the People's Advocate had ceased by 1884, and the National Republican's digitized run ends in May 1888. The same sitting of the county court removed every previously appointed policeman except Robert Walker (alexandriagazette1888rule); whether those men were Black, whether their removal was a political purge of Readjuster-era appointees, and where Judge D. M. Chichester stood politically are all unknown, but a county court term disposes of all county business at once, so the two items sharing a sitting is weak evidence on its own.
settles: The Alexandria County court order book for 1888 at the Library of Virginia, which would carry the rule and its disposition and name the policemen removed and who replaced them, and the Board's minute books at the Center for Local History, which the 1967 compilation (arlhist1967officials) was read from; neither is online. A residence for Allen in the 1880 census would settle where he lived. The Alexandria Gazette for the weeks after 3 September 1888 would name the replacements and is searchable from here, and who elected Chichester to the bench, and when, is in the General Assembly's journals.

question: What 1982 c. 108 did to § 15.2-703. The 1952 text (vaacts1952c443) barred a member from directing or requesting an appointment or taking any part in one, and made a violation a misdemeanor costing the member his office; the 1962 recodification carries that text verbatim (vaacts1962c623), and the 1971 conforming act re-enacts §§ 15.1-674, 677 and 685 without it (vaacts1971exsess). Today's section bars only dictating, carries no penalty, and adds the sentence letting the board fully and freely discuss personnel with the manager. So c. 108 or the 1997 recodification made every one of those changes, and c. 108 is much the likelier.

settles: Charlottesville's charter history: the charter acts amending § 5.01 and its predecessors, read on HathiTrust for the years in full view

subject: localities
question: Whether the 1930 act borrowed from a model. The NML model county manager law came out after the act was signed on 20 March 1930, so the likelier template is the optional county-manager law in Gilbertson's The County (1917). The 1952 non-interference text follows the NML's 1916 Model City Charter (nml1916modelcharter) down to the misdemeanor and the forfeiture, and Richard S. Childs, chairman of the League's executive committee, spoke in Arlington on 29 September 1951 urging clarification of the Board's relationship with the manager (dailysun1951institute). The carve-out Arlington has today was in council-manager charters by 1958 (richland1958charter), but the 1927 and 1941 editions a Virginia drafter would have used are unread. Whether Arlington was the first county to adopt the form by popular vote rests on how the North Carolina counties adopted it after 1927, which is unconfirmed.
settles: The 1930 act (Acts 1930, p. 450) on HathiTrust read against Gilbertson 1917's appendix; the 1927 and 1941 Model City Charter editions; the North Carolina adoptions in Wager's County Government Across the Nation (1950)

question: What prompted 1952 c. 443, the non-interference bar, and which way the 1951 ruling behind it went. The rest of the package is traced and filed: the League of Women Voters set out the manager and county-attorney proposals on 29 September 1951 and the Arlington Civic Federation asked there for the subpoena power that became c. 162 (dailysun1951institute); the county's delegation carried the proposals that December (dailysun1951bills); and the League's president filed a 204-signature petition on 11 July 1952 that put the two manager questions on the November ballot (dailysun1952petitions). c. 443 is in neither list and was enacted outright. The Daily Sun contradicts itself on the trigger: on 19 July 1952 it says the Circuit Court ruled the Board should appoint department heads (dailysun1952petitions), and on 28 November 1951 that Judge McCarthy's ruling overruled the Board for taking the police chief's appointment away from the manager (dailysun1951policechief). The paper's digitised run begins in October 1951, after the decision, and the Evening Star for 1951 did not surface it.
settles: The Arlington Circuit Court's 1951 order, from the Center for Local History or the court's own records; or the Evening Star for the week it was handed down, once the date is known; and the Daily Sun for March and April 1952 around S 431's passage

question: The County Board's power to appoint its own County Attorney, exercised again on 2 December 2025, traces to the referendum authorised by 1952 c. 569 (vaacts1952c569), which the League of Women Voters had proposed on 29 September 1951 as a counsel separate from the Commonwealth's Attorney (dailysun1951institute). Under that act an appointed attorney serves at the Board's pleasure for no more than a year without renewal. The referendum was not among the seven questions on the 4 November 1952 ballot (dailysun1952lwv), so it was never called; and Edmund D. Campbell was already acting as the Board's counsel that autumn (paolicelli1952), so the office may predate the act and rest on something else.
settles: Whether a later session reopened the window, as 1954 c. 151 and 1958 c. 208 did for the election question, traced through the codification history of § 15.2-707's neighbours on HathiTrust; then the Daily Sun for a later vote

subject: members
question: Election results are the only source for the roster after Novack's article ends in 1994, so it holds nobody seated between 1995 and 2026 who did not win a contest. Tannia Talento, appointed on 15 July 2023 to the seat Katie Cristol resigned on 4 July, is the one member this loses, and Cristol's term runs to December 2023 in her place. Keena's workbook carries the appointment and codes Talento a Hispanic woman, and its notes column records appointments, resignations, deaths and removals from 1932 to 2026 - "Appointed on 7/15/2023 to fill seat vacated by Katie Cristol", "Removed 9/17/52" - which an election-returns document does not state. The workbook holds one sheet, with no sources column and no notes tab. What did Keena key that column from?
settles: Keena naming the document; or a roll of members and service dates from the Clerk to the County Board, which would witness 1995-2026 as Novack witnesses 1932-1994
